title: Word Parts: Prefixes, Roots and Suffixes
objective: Break medical terms into prefixes, roots and suffixes to decode unfamiliar words.
body:
Most medical terms are built from Greek and Latin parts. If you know the parts, you can decode words you have never seen.

**Root (combining form).** The core meaning, usually a body part: *cardi/o* (heart), *gastr/o* (stomach), *hepat/o* (liver), *nephr/o* and *ren/o* (kidney), *oste/o* (bone), *derm/o* (skin), *neur/o* (nerve), *pulmon/o* (lung).

**Prefix.** Comes before the root and changes its meaning: *brady-* (slow), *tachy-* (fast), *hyper-* (above/excessive), *hypo-* (below/deficient), *peri-* (around), *intra-* (within), *sub-* (under), *poly-* (many).

**Suffix.** Comes at the end and usually describes a condition or procedure: *-itis* (inflammation), *-ectomy* (surgical removal), *-otomy* (cutting into), *-ostomy* (creating an opening), *-algia* (pain), *-logy* (study of), *-emia* (blood condition), *-scopy* (visual examination).

**Decode from the end.** Read the suffix first, then the prefix, then the root. *Gastritis* = inflammation (-itis) of the stomach (gastr). *Tachycardia* = fast (tachy-) heart (cardi) condition (-ia).
examples: Appendectomy: surgical removal (-ectomy) of the appendix.
Hypoglycemia: below-normal (hypo-) sugar (glyc) in the blood (-emia).

questions.explanation: -itis means inflammation, as in tonsillitis or arthritis.

questions.stem: Bradycardia describes a heart rate that is:
questions.explanation: Brady- means slow; cardi refers to the heart.

questions.stem: Which combining form refers to the kidney?
questions.explanation: nephr/o (and ren/o) mean kidney; hepat/o means liver.
Pericardium is the sac around the heart.
Hyper- means excessive; glyc means sugar; -emia means blood condition.

title: Body Systems, Directions and Abbreviations
objective: Use anatomical directions, body-system vocabulary and common abbreviations accurately.
body:
**Directional terms** describe location relative to the body in anatomical position (standing, facing forward, palms forward).
- *Anterior/ventral*: front. *Posterior/dorsal*: back.
- *Superior*: above. *Inferior*: below.
- *Medial*: toward the midline. *Lateral*: away from the midline.
- *Proximal*: closer to where a limb attaches. *Distal*: farther from it.

**Body planes.** The *sagittal* plane divides left and right, the *frontal (coronal)* plane divides front and back, and the *transverse* plane divides top and bottom.

**System vocabulary.** Cardiovascular (heart, vessels), respiratory (lungs, airway), digestive (stomach, intestines, liver), musculoskeletal (bones, muscles), nervous (brain, spinal cord, nerves), integumentary (skin, hair, nails), urinary (kidneys, bladder), endocrine (glands and hormones).

**Common abbreviations.** *BP* blood pressure; *HR* heart rate; *NPO* nothing by mouth; *PRN* as needed; *STAT* immediately; *b.i.d.* twice a day; *t.i.d.* three times a day; *PO* by mouth. Facilities keep 'do not use' lists of error-prone abbreviations, so always follow local policy.
examples: The wrist is distal to the elbow.
A patient marked NPO before surgery should not eat or drink.

questions.stem: The knee is ____ to the ankle.
questions.explanation: Proximal means closer to the point of attachment (the hip).

questions.stem: Which plane divides the body into left and right portions?
questions.explanation: The sagittal plane runs front to back, dividing left and right.
NPO is from the Latin nil per os.

questions.stem: Which system includes the skin, hair and nails?
questions.explanation: The integumentary system covers and protects the body.
t.i.d. means ter in die, three times a day.
Medial is toward the body's midline; lateral is away from it.

questions.stem: Hormone-producing glands belong to which system?
questions.explanation: The endocrine system regulates the body with hormones.
STAT comes from the Latin statim, immediately.

flashcards.definition: Farther from the point of attachment or origin.
Divides the body into left and right portions.
Toward the front of the body.
Skin, hair, nails and associated glands.
